Anesthesiologists do not give an injection and leave the operating table. They assess anesthesia risk before surgery, induce and maintain anesthesia, continuously manage respiration, circulation, and pain, handle intraoperative emergencies, and oversee recovery and postoperative analgesia. They protect the patient's lifeline throughout surgery, suiting steady, rigorous people who handle pressure.
